# Review — cid-tiradas-120-123 (vv. 2474–2542, tiradas 120–123)

Checked: every unit's `t`/`l`/`i`/`n` against the pinned packet and conventions.md; the scan, PDF pp. 288–292
(printed 284–288), read on the image, including the four tirada rubrics and every Pidal footnote quoted in a note
(2478, 2483, 2488, 2490, 2491, 2495, 2500, 2504, 2517, 2519, 2522, 2531, 2533, 2536, 2539), and PDF p. 287 for the
labels around Minaya's *Matastes a Búcar*. I also checked the published cid-tiradas-115-117 and 118-119 (house
renderings and continuity), the `l` usage across all published parts for Ferrando, Canpeador, ifantes, don Elvira,
mi[e] and Valençia la mayor, the notes at vv. 473 and 992 on *ela/elas*, and QUESTIONS.md on the double label 2455.
Pass 2 covered all 45 new gloss entries and the `__broaden__` block, with old entries taken from known-forms.json.

All footnote quotations and all four rubrics match the print. The `t` fields joined by "\n" equal the 69 packet
verses in print order; no `t` was changed; every `l` has as many lines as its `t` (verified by script after editing).

## Pass 1: units.json

1. 2493 · n · style. The note read "he = I have: aver, … as a full verb. aver here the noun": the two *aver*s sat side by side and could be confused. Rewritten: "he, 'I have', present of aver as a full verb …; the aver after it is the noun, 'wealth, goods'."
2. 2505 · l, n · weak. "Valençia [la mayor]" was "[the greater]". The house form in published `l` (vv. 2105, 2160) is "Valençia the great". Changed to "[the great]" in `l` and in the note.
3. 2507 · i · weak. "they won between them the worth of five thousand marks": *amos a dos* is just 'both', and whether the sum is joint or each man's is not said. Changed to "the two of them won the worth of five thousand marks".
4. 2507 · n · weak (drafter's doubt, 2510). The note offered two equal readings of *muchos tienen por ricos ifantes de Carrión*. Reading *muchos* as an adverb with the Infantes as subject ("count themselves rich") would need a *se* (cf. *ques tienen por casadas*), and the line has none. Rewritten so the main reading is 'many hold the Infantes rich', *tener por* + object without the personal *a*; the other reading is called less likely but not impossible.
5. 2518 · l · error (house rule, drafter's doubt, 2519). "the my wif[e]" put the bracket on the wrong word. Pidal's restored *e* belongs to *mi[e]*, and English "my" has no counterpart for it, so no bracket is used (as at v. 277, "the my soul"). The same applies to "th[e] my daughters" for *la[s]*, where the restored *s* has no counterpart in "the". Both are now plain: "the my wife worthy", "both the my daughters".
6. 2524 · n · error. "abredes … the split-off future of aver written together" contradicts itself. It now reads "abredes = avredes (habréis), 'you will have', future of aver, the vowel of the infinitive dropped."
7. 2527 · l · style. "[Infante] Fernan[do]" modernized the name in `l`. The house keeps the manuscript form *Ferrando* in `l` (vv. 1900, 2267, 2339, 2348). Changed to "Ferran[do]".
8. 2530 · n · error (drafter's doubt, footnote 2522). The note said "The print labels Minaya's line 2457". On the image (PDF p. 287) *Matastes a Búcar* has no label. The print's labels are 2455 (on "Grado a Dios …") and 2460, and counting from them puts it at 2457, which is how the published 118-119 numbers it (unit 2457). The drafter's point is right: Pidal's own "v. 2458" is the number the line takes if the second 2455 is a slip for 2456, as QUESTIONS.md (2026-11-24) argues. The footnote is independent support for that verdict. The parenthesis was rewritten to say this, and the vague "discussed in the last part" now names cid-tiradas-118-119.
9. 2532 · l, i, n · error. *quien f[o]ra en alcanço* was rendered "had-b[e]en" / "had been" and glossed "fuera, 'had been'". Pidal's own note gives 'había ido', so this is *ir*, which shares the forms of *ser* (the glossary's *fora* is already 'had gone'). Changed to `l` "had-g[o]ne", `i` "or who had gone in the pursuit?", and the note now says "the -ra pluperfect of ir … 'had gone'".
10. 2532 · l · style. "Dí[da]go nor Fernando" rendered *Ferrando* as "Fernando". The house keeps "Ferrando" in `l`, so this was changed.
11. 2535 · l · weak. *escarmentando* was "teaching", which is weaker than the note's own 'chastise, teach a hard lesson'. Changed to "chastising".
12. 2535 · n · weak (drafter's doubt, 2536). The note leaned to *elas* = e + las. Pidal quotes *elas noches e los dias* as one phrase ('siempre, continuamente') and prints no circumflex, which is his mark for two words run together (ên, lâ). At v. 473 he admits *ela* as the archaic article. Rewritten: most likely the archaic full article (= las), set against *los días*. The note also says that e + las is possible (as the note to v. 992 took it), that the sense is Pidal's 'always' either way, and that the form is uncertain. The `l` ("the nights and the days") already fits.
13. 2538 · i · weak. "(brothers indeed, and alike in heart)" added a gloss the text does not have. Changed to "(true brothers they are)", which keeps the irony of *veramientre son hermanos* without spelling it out.
14. 2538 · n · style. "Adam traduce bien … with Pidal's reading" stated as fact what Pidal implies. Changed to "(presumably as Pidal reads the line)".
15. 2489 · l · style. The `l` added a ";" after "camels in-plenty" where the `t` (*camellos largos*) has no punctuation. Removed.

Checked and confirmed, no change:
- **2481** (drafter's doubt): *aver [n]os [han]* as the split future (infinitive + clitic + *han* = *nos avrán*) is the only grammatical analysis, and the note already says the exact turn is uncertain.
- **2520**: *don Elvira* is kept in `l` and is "Doña Elvira" in `i`, as in every published part (vv. 2075, 2086, 2097, 2160, 2180, 2196).
- **Order notes**: 2508 is printed before 2507; 2522–2523 are printed after 2530, and the second label really is printed "2553".
- **2540**: the speech opens —“ with no closing quote in this part; tirada 124 opens again with —“ (*Pidamos*).
- **Uncertain readings**: the raised dot after *dos* (2479), Ca[di] and Dí[da]go italic extent, se[d]iense, 2483, and 2481 are all flagged as uncertain.
- **House renderings**: Minaya, Álvar Fáñez / Albar in `l`, Don Jerome, Valencia / Valençia, born in a good hour, onor (estate; lands and lordship) vs ondra / honor (honour), King Búcar, Morocco, Diego and Fernando in `i`.
- **Remembered translation**: I found no English in `i` that reads like a remembered translation.

Refused:
- 2499 `i` "though I have no such thought" for *ca non lo pie[n]sso yo* (note: *ca* 'for'). A literal "for" makes no sense in English here, and the note explains the turn. Kept.
- Canpeador rendered "Campeador" in `l` (2492, 2506). Published parts are mixed (6 normalized, 3 kept), so there is no house rule to enforce. Kept.
- "Infantes" capitalized in `l`. Published parts are mixed (20 lower-case, 12 capitalized). Kept.
- 2489: at high zoom the *a* of Ca[di]erónle may also be italic. The pinned text cannot be changed here, and the note already says the extent is uncertain. Left; it could go to the establishing run.
- 2493 `i` "wealth and land, gold and lands and lordship" repeats "land(s)", but "lands and lordship" is the house rendering of onor. Kept.

## Pass 2: gloss.json

1. abrám · error. "contracted from avrán" was wrong: the form is *avrán* spelled with b and final -m. The entry also said "sense of the construction from context" where Pidal gives the sense ('que yo les asalte'). Both fixed.
2. cuñados · error. The entry gave "brother-in-law … 'brothers-in-law'", against Pidal's note (in general 'pariente por afinidad'). It now reads "kinsman by marriage, in-law", with Pidal's gloss.
3. sediense · error. "with n of -ién lost before the clitic" was false, since the n is there (*sedien* + *se*). Rewritten: imperfect 3rd pl. *sedien*, unaccented as printed, + enclitic *se*.
4. veramientre · error. "vera + -miente" was wrong; the suffix is -mientre, the old form of -mente.
5. lidiaran · weak. "Latin -arant" was imprecise, and "here after veo …" pinned the entry to one line. Now: from the Latin pluperfect in -(av)erant, with its old pluperfect value; modern lidiaran is imperfect subjunctive.
6. lidiara · weak. The same Latin fix; the gloss now gives 'had fought' first.
7. honor · weak. "learned spelling" was an unsupported claim. Now: spelled with h-, in the sense of ondra, not onor 'estate'.
8. escarmentando · weak. "teasing" was an invented sense, followed by "exact sense from context". Now: chastising, punishing, teaching a hard lesson (cf. the glossary's escarmentar 'to chastise, punish').
9. ovier · style. Pidal's gloss 'a quien yo quisiere' was added, and the "final -e dropped (= oviere)" noted.
10. pensad · style. Pidal's 'cuidaos de' was added.
11. detardamos · style. "linger" was added and the modern equivalent corrected to *nos demoramos*.
12. __broaden__ · weak. Known entries did not cover this part's use, so six broadens were added (old entry kept whole + " · also …"):
    - *elas*: the possible archaic article, with Pidal's 'siempre'.
    - *salto*: 'assault', with Pidal's 'les asalte'.
    - *contado*: plain 'counted', since the old entry has only 'renowned'.
    - *sabor*: aver sabor 'to long for, wish', with Pidal's 'quisiere'.
    - *mayor*: *la mayor*, the epithet of Valencia.
    - *tienen*: *tener por* 'hold (someone) to be'.

The rest were checked against the form and found right: vencieron, ondrados, prisiessen, cadierónle, azémilas, camellos, serién, minguado, arranco, mezquitas, quiçab, temen, piensso, paguen, lidiaron, valía, crió, recibiólos, valemos, abraçen, casamientos, abredes, lidiado, matamos, traydor, provado, tenémoslo, saluo, fallavan, juegos, levantando, conssejaron, fáblaron and despender. The keys equal the novel-form tokens plus `__broaden__` (verified by script), and every broaden begins with the known entry exactly.

Refused:
- recibiólos lemma "recebir". It is kept, because the shared glossary already uses recebir/reçebir for this verb.
- The drafter's `iffantes` broaden is redundant: the known entry already has "a young man of noble birth". It is kept because it sharpens the sense ('son of a noble house') and harms nothing.
